### Part 4
```{r}
library(fortunes)
fortune()
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
```

#### Vectors: a way to store multiple values in R. All values must be the same type (as categorized above)
```{r}
my_first_vector <- c(1, 5, 9)
print(x = my_first_vector)

num_cells_after_1 <- 1432
num_cells_after_2 <- 7543


cell_ID <- c("CX1", "CX2")
treated <- c(TRUE, FALSE)
num_cells_before <- c(5415, 8123)
num_cells_after <- c(num_cells_after_1, num_cells_after_2)
print (paste(cell_ID, treated, num_cells_before, num_cells_after))
print(cell_ID[2])
```
```{r}
all_my_pets <- c("dog", "horse", "guinea pig", "chicken", "cat")
birds=all_my_pets[4]
print(birds)
```
In vectors, many operations can be applied to an entire vector at once.

#### Data Frames
Common type of data structure. A table with rows and columns. Each row is a single sampling unit, each column is a specific piece of info. We use tibble() here.
```{r}
cell_IDs <- c("CX1", "CX2")
treateds <- c(TRUE, FALSE)
num_cells_befores <- c(5415, 8123)
num_cells_afters <- c(1432, 7543)
my_data_frame <- tibble (
  cell_ID = cell_IDs,
  treated = treateds, 
  num_cells_before = num_cells_befores, 
  num_cells_after = num_cells_afters
)
gt(my_data_frame)

```

```{r}
my_data_frame <- tibble (
  cell_ID = c("CX1", "CX2"),
  treated = c(TRUE, FALSE), 
  num_cells_before = c(5415, 8123), 
  num_cells_after = c(1432, 7543)
)
print(my_data_frame)

```
